VIII — Founder's Note

Why I quit
collagen.

I'm thirty-eight. I've been rolling for twelve years. The first nine were unremarkable — train hard, recover, train hard again.

The last three were a slow surrender. Fingers that wouldn't grip a gi by round four. An elbow that "wasn't right" two days a week, then three, then most of the time. The reflex of grabbing the ibuprofen bottle before training. The honest reckoning, sitting in a physical therapist's waiting room for the third time, that this trajectory ends with me off the mats.

I went looking for the actual mechanism — not the marketing claim. Why do tendons fail with age, and what cell rebuilds them? The answer pointed to fibroblasts. The intervention that activated them pointed to one plant. The supplement market wasn't offering it as a single ingredient at a clinical dose — so we built it.

This report is my work product. Tap-Less is the protocol I take every morning.

— Filed by the founder.

XI — Common Questions

Honest answers.

Most users feel the first change — less post-training stiffness, fewer "bad-morning" days — at around the two-week mark. Structural change in connective tissue takes longer. Plan for the full 12-week protocol before evaluating whether to continue.

Three different mechanisms. Turmeric reduces inflammation systemically — useful, but it doesn't rebuild anything. Collagen peptides provide raw amino-acid substrate — useful, but only if the fibroblast is awake to assemble it. Glucosamine targets cartilage, not tendon.

Moringa is the only one of these that re-activates the synthesis cell itself.

Two capsules per day. One serving. Take with a meal. On training days, 30–60 minutes pre-roll. On rest days, with morning food. Take daily, including rest days.

Moringa has a long-established safety record with no known interaction at typical supplemental doses with NSAIDs, testosterone-replacement, or commonly-stacked supplements (creatine, collagen, omega-3, magnesium). If you're on prescription medication — particularly anticoagulants or diabetes medication — run it past your physician first.
